*   The deepEqual function must return false when comparing two objects where the same key holds an empty array in one object and an empty plain object in the other (e.g., { items: [] } vs { items: {} } and vice versa).

## Summary

Fixed the bug in `src/utils/deepEqual.ts`. 

**Root cause:** When comparing `[]` and `{}`, both have zero keys so the length check passed, and neither triggered the existing `isEmptyObjectWithCustomPrototype` guard (an empty array fails its `!Array.isArray` clause; an empty plain object fails its `!isPlainObject` clause). The key loop then ran zero iterations and returned `true`.

**Fix:** Added a targeted check that returns `false` when one value is an empty array and the other is an empty plain object (in either order). This is deliberately narrow — it does **not** reject a non-empty array vs a plain object with matching keys, preserving the existing sparse-array-vs-plain-object behavior (issue #13346, test at line 93). Because nested values recurse through `deepEqual`, the nested `{ items: [] }` vs `{ items: {} }` cases are covered automatically.

Note: `src/__tests__/utils/deepEqual.test.ts` currently has a pre-existing parse error under `yarn jest` (TypeScript annotations not transformed) unrelated to my source change — per instructions, the verification system applies test patches automatically, so I left the tests untouched and verified the logic with a standalone reproduction of the full function.
